title: Can Elon Musk really put AI datacentres in space? - The Latest
byline: Zoe Hitch, Dan Milmo, Leonore Schick, Michael Safi, Angus Neale
excerpt: The Trump administration has approved Elon Musk’s plan to launch one million satellites into orbit to create datacentres in space. SpaceX argues the project could reduce the impact of datacentres on Earth as the AI industry grows. But how realistic is the plan and what could the consequences be? Michael Safi speaks to Guardian global technology editor Dan Milmo
content_html: The Trump administration has approved Elon Musk’s plan to create datacentres in space. US federal regulators have authorised the launch of one million Starmind orbital satellites, which are built by Musk’s SpaceX, to process data in space. Supporters argue the project will be more energy-efficient and reduce the environmental impact of datacentres on Earth as the AI industry grows. But how realistic is the plan and what could the consequences be? Michael Safi speaks to Guardian global technology editor Dan Milmo
